correctness.rationale: PASS. With t=log(omega tau0), a=log r and c=cosh a, the three Debye terms become Δepsilon/2 times sech(t-a)+sech t+sech(t+a), an even function. Writing z=cosh t≥1 gives G_c(z)=1/z+2cz/(z²+c²-1). Its derivative equals a strictly negative prefactor times Q_c(z²/(c²-1)) with Q_c(u)=(1+2c)u²+2(1-c)u+1 and discriminant 4c(c-4). For c<4 no roots, c=4 a double root at z²=5 gives two non-extremal horizontal shoulders, and c>4 two simple roots z²>1 generate exactly two minima and two outer maxima around the ever-strict central maximum. Thus r*=4+sqrt15 and the complete explicit extrema coordinates. Expansion near c=4 gives ±(sqrt5/6)sqrt(c-4) splitting, while large-r positions are (1/2)log r and log r and loss minimum is asymptotic to 2Δepsilon/sqrt r. Independent numerical root/discriminant checks agree; finite computations not used for arbitrary-r proof.
